notice: Pending-events contract: one file per event the human must attend, only in gtt-domain/pending/. Data only. The engine (.gtt/scripts/gtt_pending.py), the hook (.claude/hooks/pending-watch.py) and the CLI (gtt pending, gtt answer) read it; none carries these texts, limits or numbers of its own.
threshold: Settle simple, reversible questions yourself: take the simplest option and continue. Ask the human only decisions that are theirs (account, key, money, legal, product, governed file) and that governed context cannot settle. Tell them a decision only when it changes scope, time, cost, security or the design. Questions reach the human in the chat, as one batch of up to four, each in the form of its event (the topic, the question, numbered options each with what you will do, the recommended one first): run `gtt-pending.sh show` and show its output. The event file is the silent record, one per event, written only through gtt-pending.sh: do not announce files; mention one only for a proposal or something to review outside the chat. Plain words, one idea per line, for a person who was not in the session: every question carries `--context` (what it is about) and `--term "b2 = what it is"` for any code or name they could not guess; the engine refuses it otherwise. With no answer, use the recommended option. Apply each answer where it belongs, then mark it with `done`. Open a batch with `@gtt · Needs you (N)`. Never write the human's answer.

rev.note: A review (REV) is one decision on an inbox entry (a PROP or an architect's ADR draft). It never resolves itself: there is no default and no 7 days of silence, `gtt answer ok` is for decisions only, and it keeps the sha256 of the entry it was opened on, so an answer is refused if the entry changed. It is written only by the inbox engine, through this one; the answer reaches the entry and its idea through the engine. The text of its options is inbox.json -> labels.

limits.note: A question may use ask_max_lines (each option carries a description line); a decision max_lines. The limits apply to what the engine writes (up to and including the answer label); the answer area is the human's and is only checked for key shapes and its line length.

todo.note: What waits for the person, in one plain line per kind: what to do, where, and what happens. Fixed texts written by the engine (no tokens): the same in every event, so the person always finds it in the same place. ASK and REV carry it in their file; Sonar shows it on every card of `I need you`.

ask.en: Answer with the number of an option, or write your own answer. If you do not, the recommended option is used.
ask.es: Responde con el número de una opción, o escribe tu propia respuesta. Si no lo haces, se usa la recomendada.

provide.en: Give it outside the chat (a key goes in .env.local, an account in your own panel) and tell the agent it is done.
provide.es: Entrégalo fuera del chat (una clave va en .env.local, una cuenta en tu propio panel) y avísale al agente que está hecho.

review.en: Decide on this proposal with the number of an option. Nothing changes in the design until you answer, and it never answers by itself.
review.es: Decide sobre esta propuesta con el número de una opción. Nada cambia en el diseño hasta que respondas, y nunca se responde sola.

promote.en: Review what changes and run the command in your terminal. Only you promote: the agent prepared it and cannot apply it.
promote.es: Revisa qué cambia y ejecuta el comando en tu terminal. Solo tú promueves: el agente lo preparó y no puede aplicarlo.

ratify.en: Approve it in your terminal with the command shown. Only you approve: until then it stays proposed.
ratify.es: Apruébalo en tu terminal con el comando que se muestra. Solo tú apruebas: hasta entonces queda propuesto.

adopt.en: Adopt this draft into the inbox with the command shown, or leave it where it is.
adopt.es: Adopta este borrador en la Bandeja con el comando que se muestra, o déjalo donde está.

blocked.en: A Story cannot continue until you decide what blocks it. Open it and answer, or tell the agent how to unblock it.
blocked.es: Una Story no puede continuar hasta que decidas qué la bloquea. Ábrela y responde, o dile al agente cómo destrabarla.

plain.note: An event is read by a person who was not in the session and may not know the project's words. Every ASK carries `In plain words` (what this is about, in a few plain sentences, never a restatement of the question) and, for any code, acronym or name a person could not guess (b2, S3, EC2, a library, an internal name), a `Terms` line `term = what it is`. The engine refuses an ASK whose question or options use such a code that neither line explains. Ids the page links (STORY-467, EPIC-004, ASK-014) and plain version words (v1) need no explanation.

necessity.note: A question is asked only when something cannot continue without the answer. Account, key, money and legal questions are always the human's; a product or governed one must name the Story or Epic it blocks, or the agent settles it with the recommended option. A review (REV) does not need to block a Story: it waits, weighs by the hours it would add, and is reminded every reminder_hours.

en.chat: Talk about it in the chat: say «let's talk»
en.answer_hint: (ok, or tell me what to change)

en.tail: Answer here in the chat, or with gtt answer
en.tail_fyi: Say «ok» or tell me what to change
en.plain_missing: write --context: what this is about in plain words, for someone who was not in the session (at least {n} characters, not a copy of the question)
en.plain_terms: explain {codes} in --context or with --term "{first} = what it is" (a code or name a person could not guess)
en.batch_tail: Answer each one with its number (e.g. «14: 1, 15: 2»), or write what you prefer.
en.review_tail: A review is answered with an option number only: «15: 1» here, or gtt answer 15 1; for anything else, say it and the agent will propose again.

es.tail: Responde aquí en el chat, o con gtt answer
es.plain_missing: escribe --context: de qué se trata, en simple, para alguien que no estuvo en la sesión (al menos {n} caracteres, sin repetir la pregunta)
es.plain_terms: explica {codes} en --context o con --term "{first} = qué es" (un código o nombre que una persona no podría adivinar)
es.batch_tail: Responde cada una con su número (p. ej. «14: 1, 15: 2»), o escribe lo que prefieras.
es.review_tail: Una revisión se responde solo con el número de una opción: «15: 1» aquí, o gtt answer 15 1; para otra cosa, dilo y el agente propondrá de nuevo.

rules.statement: an event is at most max_lines lines of at most max_chars characters (what the engine wrote)

a question is one line that ends in «?», has a short Topic, 2 or 3 numbered options each with a one-line description, exactly one recommended, and the two closing lines (something else, talk about it in the chat)
a question carries a type of the list; a decision carries an `Affects` of the list
a decision has three lines (what, why, where it landed) and every `Where it landed` exists
an answer never looks like a key; a key goes in .env.local
the name, the number and the heading of an event agree, and no number repeats
a question is necessary: a product or governed question names the Story or Epic it blocks, no question repeats an open one, and at most max_open_asks questions are open at once (answer those first)

a review (REV) names its entry, carries the sha256 of it, has 2 to 5 numbered options each with a one-line description, exactly one recommended, no closing lines, and at most rev.max_lines lines of rev.max_chars characters

a question explains itself to someone who was not in the session: an `In plain words` line (at least plain_min_chars) and every code or name in the question, the options or the topic (b2, S3...) explained in it or in `Terms`; the engine refuses to create one that does not
an answered event that nobody marked is waiting to be applied
